claims.text: MailKit's SmtpClient.Timeout (inherited from MailService) is a timeout in milliseconds for network operations with the server; when an operation gets no answer within it, the call throws an exception.
claims.source_hint: MailKit API docs: MailService.Timeout property ("timeout for network streaming operations, in milliseconds")

claims.text: MailKit's Timeout applies to each network operation (connect, each read/write of the SMTP exchange), not to the whole SendAsync as one total, so a send whose steps are each slow but answered can exceed it in total.
claims.source_hint: MailKit API docs: MailService.Timeout; SmtpClient.ConnectAsync remarks; MailKit source SocketUtils.ConnectAsync (timeout argument)

The stoppingToken that BackgroundService.ExecuteAsync receives is signalled when the host shuts down; it is not signalled by a slow call.

claims.text: SendDueAsync (NotificationSender.cs @ stage-2 lines 47-59) claims up to BatchSize (10) rows, awaits SendOneAsync for each row in a foreach before the next, and calls CompleteAsync once after the loop.
Because sends of a batch are awaited one after another, one send that waits until its timeout delays every later email of the same batch by that wait.

claims.text: On a timeout MailKit drops the connection, but nothing asks the mail server to undo what it received: a server that had the whole email and only replied late to the message may still deliver it.

claims.source_hint: MailKit MailService.Timeout; StackExchange.Redis 'Configuration'; Npgsql 'Connection String Parameters'

claims.text: Without a timeout, a call to a server that accepted the connection but never answers may wait indefinitely or until a lower-level limit (the library's own default or the OS's TCP handling) ends it; that limit, if any, varies and cannot be counted on to be short.

A longer timeout fails fewer slow calls but makes each stuck call hold its caller (and, in a sequential batch, everything behind it) for longer; a shorter one fails some calls that would have succeeded.

A library default is chosen by its authors for all users of the library, not for one application; when an app leaves it unset, its value is still the app's effective timeout, and the library's documentation for that setting gives it.

A stopped Mailpit accepts no connection, so no timeout is involved. If paused (cgroup freezer), nothing answers, so each MailKit send waits about the 10 s Timeout and throws; SendOneAsync/RecordFailure handle it as any failure.
